hook_text: On a cold winter morning, you can sometimes see a brown blanket of dirty air lying over Johannesburg.
clip_script: Six o'clock in the morning in Gauteng. Minibus taxis hoot and race to the rank. A long red bus glides along its own lane. A fast train whooshes past. On the highway, trucks carry food, fuel and furniture, bumper to bumper. And from every exhaust pipe, grey fumes puff into the cold air. From a hilltop, you can see it: a brown haze hanging over the city. Transport keeps the city moving, but the air pays the price.
visual_style: Whiteboard city skyline with taxis, a bus, a train and trucks along the bottom, exhaust clouds rising and joining into a brown layer, with a cold-air lid drawn above.
mood: Busy and noisy, then serious and thoughtful.
pacing: Fast and crowded for the morning rush, then slow down to look at the haze.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and count the different kinds of transport you see on your way home.
